look_here_first: FLORIDA PASPALUM: tall stout native-grass-type bunch with a FEW long racemes and relatively broad rounded flattened spikelets, generally around 3.5–5 mm in regional treatments. The NEW David Stang flowering-head photograph shows three slender spikelet-bearing branches; the older original photo shows the large basal tuft. Together they teach habit plus head, but actual measured spikelets and fine glumes are still absent.

crew_field_steps: Recognize and photograph the sizeable erect broad-leaved bunch; current photo shows the leafy habit only.
Find a mature flowering head with multiple long one-sided racemes; count branches on a SINGLE culm and show complete axis.
Measure and photograph the relatively broad rounded oval spikelets with a mm ruler, and check leaf blade/sheath ligule before separating from dallisgrass and P. pubiflorum.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Full flowering culm from base to complete mature seedhead.
Two mature racemes photographed from side and face with scale.
Broad oval mature spikelets plus glume/hair macro at mm scale.
Leaf sheath/collar membrane and vegetative habit paired with P. dilatatum.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Compare Florida paspalum's broad large roundish spikelets and few racemes against smaller 2.7–3.2 mm P. pubiflorum. Both can have multiple racemes; don't conclude species from grass size or a garden photograph. Dallisgrass should have distinctive long marginal spikelet hairs.
do_not_use_alone: Number of racemes without the entire flowering axis
Habitat, height, or vegetative tuft in isolation
Microscopic glume hairs or spikelet length inferred from a photo without scale

visual_comparison.title: Paspalum floridanum — photographed field ID and look-alikes
visual_comparison.subtitle: Photos already in the Hays library, inspected individually. Annotations point ONLY to visible shapes/parts; small hairs/glumes and exact species determinations await specimen proof.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: COUNT COMPLETE RACEMES → MEASURE 5 RIPE SPIKELETS → CHECK MARGINAL HAIRS → ROOTED BASE/COLLAR. DALLIS few large silky; VASEY many small silky; FLORIDA few big round; PUBIFLORUM smaller oval; SETACEUM narrow variable; DISTICHUM two + real stolons.

items.why_it_matters: Florida paspalum tends to have big coarse basal clumps with relatively few long racemes and large often rounded spikelets. Dallisgrass generally has conspicuous long silky hairs fringing its large spikelets; vaseygrass often has much more numerous finer racemes with smaller spikelets. P. pubiflorum commonly has smaller 2.7–3.2 mm spikelets, and pubescence needs careful comparison.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Paspalum: what to inspect
steps: NEW photograph shows several intact green flowering branches, but no 1-mm scale. On site, capture the rooted tuft and same-plant full head, then 5 mature broad rounded spikelets with actual scale and upper-glume margin detail.
First show the WHOLE head, then ONE one-sided raceme and attached spikelets. Never treat a photograph of one branch as total raceme count.
Obtain a real intact mature spikelet and measure it with 1-mm reference; use margin hair pattern and glumes to separate close Paspalum taxa.
Photograph blade/sheath joint and same-plant rootstock; knotgrass needs actually rooted horizontal stolons, not merely a low mat.
If plant photo is source-labelled only, keep identity tentative and leave existing county-native fields unchanged.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Florida paspalum tends to have big coarse basal clumps with relatively few long racemes and large often rounded spikelets. Dallisgrass generally has conspicuous long silky hairs fringing its large spikelets; vaseygrass often has much more numerous finer racemes with smaller spikelets. P. pubiflorum commonly has smaller 2.7–3.2 mm spikelets, and pubescence needs careful comparison.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Gross photo structures are references, NOT expert confirmation. Even new licensed images are PROVISIONAL — USER PHOTO REVIEW PENDING and not proof of Hays County presence.
